rubric.rationale: Reassessed D1; other authority contracts carried forward. Missing newer evidence cannot make an older PASS current; all four boundaries still validate authority and applicable inputs.

dispositions.detail: A historical evidence-loss barrier rejects old proof at or before a loss position. Known gate loss affects that gate; unknown root loss affects every older gate. Focused root/output regressions reject the old PASS and admit newly executed proof; missing bytes remain absent and visible.

JSON parsing exceptions are replaced with fixed malformed-output diagnostics. Outer and nested Claude, Codex, fenced input and execution-summary paths were inspected/tested; direct read-only parser probes exposed no sentinel text.
Failure to access a configured feature home reaches the supported deny response. Both recognized native command payload forms are covered. Hook recognition and activation limitations remain explicit.

Automatic required history no longer has a 64-record cutoff. The focused fixture retains 66 original/closure records and reconsiders 33 closed findings. Explicit caller selection and actual transport byte bounds remain; neither imposes a fixed remediation-round halt.

Review of pt3T4x independently found retention referencing executeGates-local applicabilityMemo from a separate helper; its catch silently skipped every completion proof. Read-only probe showed PASS, zero currentResult calls and empty completion selection. The final successor creates a helper-local Map, uses it for inventory and completion scans, and persists both inventories. The updated actual all-gates integration verifies finalization/release references and passes. Separate milestone checks contained the prior issue; no completion bypass had been established.
Prior broader-history export defect remains fixed. Repository-scope guards and export isolation are unchanged; interacting history collection was inspected.
Prior omission of affected closed findings remains fixed. Independent relevance assessment and justified group carry-forward remain enforced; D4 regression exercises the larger closure set.
Fresh self-contained proof can replace missing applicability while history gaps remain visible. D1 now prevents old PASS resurrection; original bytes are not fabricated.
Earlier nonzero provider error sanitization plus D2 shared parser sanitization closes the observed raw diagnostic paths.

Frozen host capability matrix, native manifests and subprocess event/deny evidence support the narrow implemented hook contract. They explicitly do not claim candidate installation/trust or a real intercepted model event.

limitations: This is a standalone independent local assessment, not formal installed-protocol passage, release approval, host activation certification or production validation. The evaluator did not implement any assessed source. The original independent context was created with inheritedTurns 0; this recheck retains its own earlier review context and implementer claims, rather than claiming a new conversation for each delta.

Only supplied frozen snapshots, their requirements and retained evidence were read. No network, credentials, other workspace history or implementation edits were used. Official host documentation URLs are retained evidence, not freshly browsed verification.

Full CLI evidence reports 238 passes, one optional live-provider skip, zero failures; desktop reports 172 passes. Those broad runs predate the final helper-local memo/retention-reference correction. Their unchanged-path conclusions are carried forward after the exact two-file successor diff was inspected.

The six focused regressions include test-only additions made after the broad CLI run began (missing-output loss variant and summary sanitization). They all pass. Final successor coverage is the one expanded all-gates completion test, passing, plus repeated native lint/build validation; a complete CLI/desktop rerun on the successor was not supplied.

Earlier actual independent-provider and Electron runtime receipts support unchanged consumer/provider behavior; they are historical smoke, not new live executions of the final digest. The optional live-provider test remained skipped in the broad CLI run.

Native hook evidence is subprocess/host-contract smoke with documented supported capability, not a real model event under an installed and trusted candidate plugin. Direct recognized gh pr merge forms are covered; indirect scripts, alternate clients, disabled hooks and arbitrary external actions are outside that interception claim.

The manifest lists sourceDigest sha256:b0c15462ebf9c76a43eed525b915242ead5e2b1d340c5c0276526e72ca341229. All 367 listed source file hashes were independently checked and matched. Build sourceCommit metadata names starting HEAD for an uncommitted candidate, not its reviewed source identity or a released version.

Assessment covers the approved pre-merge requirements and changed-code interactions. Passing means no supported remaining material defect was established in this scope; it does not assert exhaustive absence of defects or newly execute every retained test.
